verdict.rationale: RudderStack's docs describe an open-source version that runs as a standalone system needing only PostgreSQL, with both a data plane and a control plane. That shows the product itself supports self-hosting. However, the evidence does not show which core features (e.g., Profiles, Reverse ETL, Audiences, MCP) the self-hosted version includes, and it gives no deployment or operations guidance, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: documented feature parity between self-hosted and cloud, self-hosting deployment instructions (Docker/Kubernetes), independent hands-on self-hosting reports.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: The open source version of RudderStack is a standalone system dependent only on a database (PostgreSQL). It consists of 2 major components: data plane and control plane
